tickets.summary: K-3401 NDE bearing vibration rose from 2.1 to 4.6 mm/s in six weeks and remains upward, indicating high failure likelihood despite being below alarm.
tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist today: inspect NDE bearing/alignment, correct findings, then verify vibration meets limits and has stabilized. Obtain source-required attention today. Repeat vibration spectrum and trend check. Review failure mode and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Vibration more than doubled over six weeks, with a growing 1x component and no plateau. This is strong active progression, but not confirmed function loss or imminent failure.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this single export-compressor train has no spare or workaround and would send the platform to recycle, cutting production within an hour.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed its first weekly-test start, then started after 8 seconds and reached rated pressure; 22.8 V at rest suggests a starting-system deficiency.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect batteries, starting air and circuit; correct found defects under fire-protection authority; retest start and delivery. Check deviation record. Confirm fire scenarios and exposure. Test FW-8101 pressure and flow. Test batteries, air and circuit. Verify first-attempt start and delivery.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Required starting function failed on the first test attempt. The successful retry and rated discharge confirm subsequent operation but do not erase the observed start failure; starting problems are recurrent.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start would remove one safety-critical firewater pump from demand service. Its N+1 partner later delivered 9.2 barg against 11 barg design with flow unmeasured, so partner capability cannot be fully credited.

tickets.summary: CUI at window 2 near the low-point drain reduced flowline wall to 6.2 mm, below the 7.4 mm minimum; containment loss is not reported but active degradation is advanced.
tickets.recommended_action: Expose and map CUI extent; integrity engineer to assess/dispose, repair as approved, then verify pressure integrity. Check release and personnel exposure. Map CUI extent and remaining life.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Wet insulation, heavy scaling and 6.2 mm wall against a 7.4 mm minimum establish advanced active CUI, creating a strong near-term containment-loss precursor without proving current loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Containment failure would release hydrocarbon from a full-wellhead-pressure production flowline with no redundancy, supporting severe personnel and process exposure; release magnitude and occupancy are not established.

tickets.summary: Main-hoist rope has 6 broken wires per lay versus a 10-wire discard criterion, with poor lubrication at the maximum-radius drum section; function loss is not demonstrated.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect rope extent, lubricate deficient section, obtain lifting-authority disposition, and verify against the discard criterion. Check lift loads and personnel exposure. Confirm current rope and survey status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Six broken wires remain below the stated ten-wire discard criterion, providing supported margin, but poor lubrication at the same section is an active degradation mechanism.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the main-hoist rope would defeat the crane's load-handling function without redundancy; loss of crane service prevents supply-boat offloads and creates a logistics problem within days.

tickets.summary: P-3305 inhibitor injection was intermittent for about 10 days after three low-pressure trips; diaphragm failure is suspected, with downstream corrosion possible within weeks.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect pump and diaphragm; repair as found under corrosion-engineer disposition and prove continuous injection at the required rate. Assess downstream integrity and exposure. Check recorded deviation status. Diagnose low-pressure trip cause. Verify required injection delivery.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The required injection function has already been repeatedly interrupted: three trips occurred in one month and injection was intermittent for about ten days. The suspected diaphragm remains an unconfirmed cause.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the sole corrosion-inhibitor pump can starve downstream carbon steel, initiating corrosion within weeks with delayed integrity consequences; production does not stop immediately.

tickets.summary: Firewater pump A delivered 9.2 barg versus 11 barg design; flow was unmeasured, so delivery capability and protection impairment remain suspected.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect pump/valves; fire-protection engineer to disposition and repair per findings. Check fire scenarios and exposure. Check impairment deviation record. Function-test FW-8102. Inspect pump/valves. Test pressure and flow to criteria.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-loaded cladding on K-3401 second-stage discharge remains attached but is likely to detach, creating a dropped-object hazard; exposure below is unknown.
tickets.recommended_action: Inspect loose cladding; secure or replace per mechanical authority, then verify retention. Check access and drop-zone exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Active wind loading and the explicit expectation that the cladding will become a dropped object support strong near-term progression, without confirming detachment has occurred.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Detachment presents a credible dropped-object hazard. Consequence is material, but personnel exposure and the drop zone are not established.

urgency.rationale: triage-policy-v3: ceil(0.7*I+0.3*L), L=8, I=5, base=6, final=7. P-SAFETY-UNKNOWN (precautionary_policy): Personnel access and exposure within the potential cladding drop zone are unknown and could change the injury consequence. Sources: finding:F-1019:finding_description.
